events.title: Bringing the Spark to Europe: Local Intelligence Powers Next Wave of Agents
events.summary: At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing its full lineup of local AI hardware. RTX Spark , which launched last week , powers personal agents on Windows PCs; DGX Spark supports developers building and scaling applications on Linux; and DGX Station serves enterprise teams running frontier workloads on Linux, with a Windows version arriving in December. Underdog Desktop Agent now available for RTX Spark DGX Spark 64GB available on Friday, Oct. 23 NVIDIA Sync to support eight DGX Sparks and add Model Launcher this month October DGX Spark software update adds Wi-Fi Assistant and updates DGX Spark Skills DGX Station improves manageability with seven new integrations DGX Station for Windows launches in December with support for many manufacturing apps and agent harnesses Three new open source reference workflows for robotics on DGX Station NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to DGX Station Recursive Flint, a new local coding model, is now available for NVIDIA local hardware Day-0 support for new Nemotron, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and FLUX.3 AI models New accelerations for llama.cpp and vLLM inference engines and a new collection of checkpoints optimized for local AI hardware. Learn more about these local AI announcements below, and check out the demos and sessions at GTC Berlin . RTX Spark Brings Personal Agents to the Windows PC RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — running personal agents, accelerated content creation and 1440p 100 frames-per-second gaming with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute. Here’s what early reviewers are saying about the platform since its October 16 release: “A dream machine for serious creators … ” — CGMag “Designed for the future of AI … ” — The Verge “An extremely capable, surprisingly portable and efficient machine … ” — PCMag Underdog , a new desktop agent app built for fully local, private AI, is also bringing its experience to RTX Spark. Powered by its Husky model-specific inference engine, Underdog runs models entirely on device, so personal agents can get work done without user data ever leaving the PC. Underdog is available now for download . To better enable developers and enthusiasts to build and customize local agents, many RTX Spark laptops come with an unlocked bootloader. During the GTC keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed off how AI agents running on RTX Spark can be used to train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B. ASUS, Dell Technologies , HP , Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI laptops are available today, with Acer coming soon. Learn more about RTX Spark , and get started with the latest RTX Spark playbooks . DGX Spark Gives Developers Room to Build New DGX Spark 64GB systems — that can run models including Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B 24GB, Qwen3.8 27B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B — start rolling out from partners on Friday, Oct. 23. When workloads require more capacity, developers can connect multiple DGX Spark systems via built-in NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant . This allows users to run advanced coding models like Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, DeepSeek v4 Flash 0731 and GLM 5.3 Flash. Now, DGX Spark supports clusters of up to eight units in manual configuration, enabling larger models, longer contexts, concurrent agents and distributed development. Ideal for small teams sharing a single cluster as a backend, with each developer running concurrent sessions against the same model, it delivers 1TB of unified memory — enough to run frontier-class models like GLM 5.3. Get started with the DGX Spark cluster playbook . NVIDIA Sync Model Launcher will also be available later this month. It simplifies access to local AI on a single DGX Spark or a cluster. With a few clicks, Model Launcher downloads a model and container suited to the configuration and connects the model to OpenCode. It automatically loads DGX Spark Skills for troubleshooting, device maintenance, access to official documentation and other workflow guidance. The October DGX Spark software update brings a new Wi-Fi Assistant that lets users switch networks when DGX Spark is running in appliance mode. Plus, DGX Spark Skills provide workflow-focused guidance in troubleshooting and device maintenance directly into NVIDIA Sync via OpenCode. DGX Spark systems are available directly from Acer , ASUS , Dell Technologies , GIGABYTE , HP , Lenovo, MSI and NVIDIA. DGX Station Puts Frontier Intelligence at the Desk For larger teams, DGX Station offers 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of AI performance, enabling developers to run advanced models like GLM 5.3 and serve 30+ users at speeds comparable to those provided by cloud models. Adding scale, NVIDIA Sync now supports DGX Station, simplifying connections between two Linux-based systems. New integrations with Absolute Security , Splunk by Cisco , Fleet Device Managemen t , Microsoft Intune , Perforce Puppet , Progress Software Chef and Tanium let IT teams manage DGX Station systems through enterprise setup, management and conformity processes, helping accelerate approvals and reduce deployment risk while minimizing time to first token. With the upcoming Windows-based systems, developers can build workflows that harness professional applications, run on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs and operate from agents that run their large language models (LLMs) on NVIDIA GB300 systems — all in one machine. DGX Station for Windows , expected from system manufacturer partners in December, extends local AI into the applications and operating environment enterprises already use. Engineers can run local models and agents in Windows-native software with access to AI models, tools and agents on the same system. DGX Station for Windows will feature support for manufacturing applications from nTop , Dassault Systèmes , Keysight Technologies , MathWorks , Rockwell Automation , Siemens , Synopsys , Unity and Altera for AI-guided design, simulation, validation and engineering automation. Users will be able to run agents using Hermes Agent , Perplexity or Aible on premises for agentic control in enterprise environments. The same local, controlled computing model extends to robotics. DGX Station gives robotics teams dedicated compute for post-training, simulation and evaluation, shortening iteration cycles without waiting for shared infrastructure. NVIDIA released three open source reference workflows that bring GPT-6 Astra, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Isaac Lab-Arena and Cosmos to NVIDIA DGX Station. Developers can use them to refine GR00T 1.7 models with reinforcement learning, train dexterous manipulation skills and post-train Cosmos world models for synthetic data generation. NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to Linux-based DGX Station. Teams can register local model endpoints in a shared catalog and access them through one OpenAI-compatible entry point.

events.title: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure
events.summary: General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. Learning through interaction requires a continuous cycle of generating experience, evaluating outcomes and updating models, requiring infrastructure that can support the entire process at scale. A5X brings Vera Rubin into Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer as an integrated system, combining compute, networking and storage to support experience-driven learning at scale. “We’re building superlearners that continually improve through their own experience,” said David Silver, founder and CEO of Ineffable Intelligence. “That demands both substantial compute and a tight connection between generating experience and training on it, so each improvement in the agent can quickly shape its next experience. Vera Rubin’s combination of compute performance and high-bandwidth connectivity, between the Vera CPU and Rubin GPUs and between the Rubin GPUs within the rack, allow us to push the scale and ambition of our reinforcement learning research further.” WPP , a London-based marketing and communications company, has also demonstrated its creative agent reference architecture on NVIDIA Vera Rubin-based A5X instances using NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA OpenShell, part of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for safe AI agents. The agents turn conversational requests into multistep creative workflows, such as video generation, upscaling and restyling, with human approval before execution. OpenShell provides governed sandboxes for agent execution, helping control access to sensitive brand assets and creative tools. In WPP’s initial tests, workloads that typically required a multi-node cluster ran on a single A5X instance. As organizations deploy agentic systems, they need to protect the proprietary models and sensitive data that power these systems — even when running on infrastructure they don’t own. Google Cloud will be among the first cloud providers to offer NVIDIA Confidential Computing at rack scale on bare metal instances such as A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Additionally, Google Cloud is making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, offering a flexible platform for confidential inference and fine-tuning. Customers including Vertebrae , Polaris Cloud and Confidential Core AI are using Confidential G4 for conversational privacy, verifiable agent execution and policy-governed enterprise intelligence. To support energy-efficient deployment at scale, Google Cloud and NVIDIA are exploring NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS capabilities for Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to help optimize performance per watt and expand capacity within available data-center power budgets. Learn more about NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Google Cloud A5X instances. events.title: TikTok is shifting advertising to YouTube after Meta says 'no thanks'
events.summary: Mark Zuckerberg's Meta has blocked Shou Zi Chew's company, TikTok, from advertising in some markets. Finn Gomez/Getty Images; Shawn Thew-Pool/Getty Images TikTok is moving on quickly after losing access to Meta's ads platform in some markets. It's shifted ad spend to YouTube, Pinterest, and mobile-app networks, according to Sensor Tower. TikTok was a prominent ad spender on Meta before its ousting on October 8. TikTok's message to Meta : If you won't take our ad dollars, your competitors will. Meta took a bold stance this month by blocking ByteDance, TikTok's parent company, from running ads on Meta apps in some markets. Why? Well, Meta's answer was pretty straightforward. It didn't want to "run ads from a competitor whose goal is to pull people off our apps." TikTok is now redirecting that ad spend elsewhere. Since the ban went into effect on October 8, TikTok has shifted its ad budgets to other platforms like YouTube and Pinterest, according to allocation estimates provided to CMO Insider by the analytics firm Sensor Tower. The share of TikTok's ad spend that went to YouTube rose to 17% between October 9 and October 16, up from 9% in the first week of October. Meanwhile, its ad spend on Pinterest grew to 9% during the same period, up from 3% in the first week of October. A majority of TikTok's spend — 58% — went to mobile-app ad networks like Google's AdMob, up from 19% at the start of October, when Meta was still an option. Meta's move against TikTok "highlights the growing intensity of the competition across the digital landscape and across the two of them," said Kate Black, EVP of social strategy at Horizon Media. "For marketers, this really just reinforces the need to be agile and build balanced media strategies — and not having all your eggs in one basket." Meta's TikTok ousting isn't unprecedented. Other platforms like Amazon have previously blocked competitors from running ads, while Twitter in late 2022 restricted users' ability to link to their accounts on social apps like Instagram and Mastodon, calling it "free promotion." "Declining promotional services to a competitor is a normal business practice across industries," a Meta spokesperson said. Meta's changes will impact advertising policies in the US, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam. For Meta, a company that pulled in $117 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026, losing one advertiser won't hurt much. Still, TikTok and ByteDance were notably prominent spenders on Meta's apps, according to Sensor Tower. Meta will also lose ad spend from third-party marketers that link to TikTok or other ByteDance properties in their ads, further increasing its potential losses. Direct-to-consumer brands that may want to drive potential customers to TikTok Shop will miss out. No Meta, no problem For TikTok, losing access to Meta's more than 3 billion monthly users is a setback. Like any social media giant, TikTok is incentivized to grow, grow, grow. Ads that target new users and drive new app downloads are part of the playbook — a strategy Meta uses to promote its own apps , like Instagram, too. One TikTok staffer focused on user acquisition, James Gao, posted a LinkedIn callout on Sunday asking people to get in touch if they had ad inventory that could help the company meet its goals. Horizon Media's Black said that while Meta controls the "lion's share" of social budgets, there are plenty of viable alternatives when it comes to using an ad to drive an action like an app download. Besides Google, YouTube, and Pinterest , marketers are increasingly turning to other platforms like Snapchat and Reddit, she said. Read the original article on Business Insider

events.title: Kvaratskhelia, Dembele and Marquinhos out injured after PSG’s win
events.summary: Kvaratskhelia out for months with a torn ACL in his right knee, while Dembele and Marquinhos suffer thigh muscle tears. Paris Saint-Germain have been handed a triple injury setback after their stunning Champions League win over Barcelona, with star players Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos forced out of action in the coming weeks. Kvaratskhelia sustained an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear in his right knee, making him unavailable for months, while forward Dembele and captain Marquinhos sustained thigh muscle injuries during the match on Tuesday. “Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days,” PSG said in a statement. Kvaratskhelia landed awkwardly after sprinting back to make a tackle on Xavi Espart early in the second half and looked in severe pain as he clutched his knee. Last year’s Ballon d’Or winner Dembele (left thigh) and Marquinhos (right thigh) are both set to miss several weeks. Dembele pulled up clutching the back of his left thigh following a run down the left in the 19th minute of the game. Kvaratskhelia and 32-year-old Marquinhos were replaced on the hour mark at the Parc des Princes, where two-time defending champions PSG won 4-2 for a third straight win in the competition. PSG coach Luis Enrique used Dembele sparingly in the French league last season and has already rested him twice in Ligue 1 this campaign. The France star, who scored six goals at the World Cup, struggled with injuries last season and had been beset by leg muscle injuries at his previous club Barcelona. The 2024-25 campaign, which led to him winning the men’s Ballon d’Or, saw Dembele playing 50 games overall in a season for the first time in his career. Kvaratskhelia injured his right ankle last season. PSG host Lyon in Ligue 1 on Sunday, with both sides level on points at the top of the standings.

events.title: I went to Paris to see Céline Dion in memory of my mom. I ended up trapped in an Uber during the riots.
events.summary: Rebecca Mac sat on Galeries Lafayette's rooftop terrace on Saturday shortly before she said the unrest began nearby. Courtesy of Rebecca Mac Rebecca Mac traveled from Manchester, UK, to Paris for a Céline Dion concert in memory of her late mother. She said she was caught in traffic near Galeries Lafayette as unrest spread through the city. Mac said hotel staff warned her against going outside, saying she was a "perfect candidate" to get mugged. This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Rebecca Mac, who owns Cosmetic Finance Group, a Manchester, UK-based aesthetics finance company, and Mc Aesthetics, a cosmetic clinic group. It has been edited for length and clarity. On Saturday, 110 demonstrations drew 550,000 people nationwide, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, including 110,000 in Paris. Organizers put the national total at 800,000. I went to Paris to see Céline Dion in memory of my mom. My mom had loved Céline for years. We had tickets to see her before the pandemic in Manchester before she died, but the show was canceled . She never got to see her perform. Friday's concert was really emotional. "All Coming Back to Me Now" and "I'm Alive" made me emotional, but "My Heart Will Go On" was the one that really made me cry. Seeing Céline felt like I was finally doing it for my mom. Little did I know, less than 24 hours later, my friend and I would be trapped in an Uber during the Paris riots . We had no way of getting out At about 3:30 p.m. on Saturday, we left Galeries Lafayette and saw what felt like a sea of people marching toward us. We were like: "Oh my god. This is crazy." We walked away and got an Uber outside Sephora. Every road the driver tried was closed. He told us to get out, but young men were running past the car, throwing things and banging. We said: "No, we're not getting out of the car in the middle of this." Rebecca Mac's Uber journey was disrupted by the riots. Courtesy of Rebecca Man Then people threw metal barriers into the road so cars could not pass. We were stuck there, panicking. Within seconds, police with riot shields charged in from the other side. We thought the crowd was coming toward us and that we were trapped in the middle. The taxi stood still for a few minutes. It felt like we had no way of getting out. Mac's Uber passed riot police standing outside a Louis Vuitton store in central Paris amid the unrest. Courtesy of Rebecca Mac The police formed a line in front of the car and cleared the barriers so traffic could move. It took about 20 minutes to get back to Le Damantin Hôtel & Spa, near the Champs-Élysées , where we were staying. Roads were sectioned off, and police on motorbikes and police vans with sirens kept passing us as we drove away. It was very stressful. It just felt very surreal and very long. We were just relieved to be back at the hotel and safe. 'Perfect targets to be mugged' Later that night, hotel staff locked the doors as we were leaving for dinner. Men in balaclavas were passing outside. A staff member told us: "You cannot go out," and said we looked like "perfect targets to be mugged." After waiting for about an hour, we decided to take a taxi to the restaurant, which was just around the corner. But it stopped across the road, where another group of six masked men was standing outside. It was quite intimidating, so we walked around parked cars to avoid getting too close to them. Rebecca Mac (right) and her friend on their way to Céline Dion's concert on Friday. Courtesy of Rebecca Mac I wanted to get home My Sunday flight to Manchester was delayed, so I booked a 9 a.m. flight to London and then an Uber home to Manchester. I kept thinking about my children. We had been to Paris a couple of years earlier for Disneyland with my little girl, my niece, and my nephew. I thought: Imagine if this had happened then. I'm so grateful I saw Céline on Friday. It is a memory I will remember forever. But I'm very upset and disappointed because I do like to go to Paris quite a lot. The whole experience made me lose my love for Paris a bit. events.title: Why are French protesters chanting ‘Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres’?
events.summary: Trump, Netanyahu and the Iran question How Iran war fallout may shape US elections For students, the slogan has come to represent a whole array of grievances that lie at the heart of the protest movement. As violent protests roil France, bringing together students demanding better educational conditions and groups rejecting the high cost of living, one chant has become an improbable rallying cry: “Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres”. The unofficial slogan does not mean much taken literally, but students have channelled a whole array of grievances that lie at the heart of the protest movement into this nonsensical expression. It is meant to mock racial stereotyping by the police. list 1 of 3 Portugal cost-of-living protesters pour back into camps cleared by police list 2 of 3 Italy approves sweeping security measures in response to protests list 3 of 3 Ballon d’Or: Which countries and players have won the most awards? Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets nationwide over the weekend, in the largest mobilisation since protests over education reforms and rising prices began last month. The protest movement has been triggered by grievances ranging from overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages to systemic inequality and lack of opportunity. Police conduct has also come under scrutiny. France’s police inspectorate, the IGPN, has opened dozens of investigations into alleged police violence since protests began. “Bismillah” is Arabic for “in the name of God”, an expression used by Muslims before beginning an activity. In French slang, it has lost some of its original meaning, becoming more akin to “let’s do it”. “C’est les ténèbres” literally translates as “it’s the darkness”, which alludes to a situation that is bleak and hopeless. The slogan therefore translates as “In the name of God, it’s the darkness”, which does not convey a clear message in and of itself. Students say the phrase is a mockery of the police force, which tried to infiltrate social media chats used by protesters to coordinate. The screenshot of a Snapchat conversation featuring the expression began circulating in early October. In it, a user named Mamadou requests to be added to a group, saying: “Hi, in the name of God, it’s the darkness. When’s the blockade, wallah, bro?” The message also featured emojis with Algerian flags. Students say the message was sent by undercover police officers attempting to infiltrate their chats by using an unconvincing mix of Arabic and slang. The claim has not been verified and French authorities have not issued any statement. Youssef El Chazli, associate professor in Arab and Mediterranean sociology at Paris 8 University Vincennes – Saint-Denis, said the phrase “reinforces an image of out-of-touch policemen filled with stereotypes”. “Such stereotypes appear to disproportionately aim at youths from Arab and African descent,” El Chazli told Al Jazeera. “This appears as one more example of how out-of-touch state agencies seem to be with the current movement.” What does the slogan tell us about the protest movement? The slogan has appeared on cardboard placards as a mockery of racial stereotypes and as a symbol of how authorities are out of touch with the realities of young people. The slogan has spread as far as Italy and Belgium, where similar protests over the high cost of living and poor education also took place over the weekend. El Chazli said satirical memes and internet trends have become tools to express political grievances during protests, which have traditionally been “inventive and creative”. “With youth mobilisations, protest creativity will draw heavily on youths’ subcultures,” he said. Discussions around Islamophobia have also taken a front seat in public debate. French authorities have been reluctant to comment publicly on a significant spike in Islamophobic acts in France. One report cited by the Reuters news agency last year showed a 72 percent increase in such incidents during the January-March quarter of 2025 compared with the same period in 2024. The French far right quickly resorted to racist language to blame Muslim youths for the violence, while United States President Donald Trump also chimed in, claiming that this is about “Islam wanting to take over”. “What used to be a nonsubject 20 years ago is now a debated point,” El Chazli said. “For younger generations, Arab and African influences have been steadily mainstreaming in youth subcultures, owing to sports and arts figures, as well as new radio shows or social media content.”

events.title: 'MAKE DEALS': Trump says data centers should pay communities a 'dividend' to win support
events.summary: President Donald Trump urged data center companies to strike financial deals with communities in a Truth Social post. "It's not crazy" to consider such a concept, Nebius Chief Revenue Officer Marc Boroditsky told CNBC. Data center development has become a political flashpoint as communities raise concerns about electricity, water and land use ahead of the November midterm elections. U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday urged data center companies to "MAKE DEALS" with local communities to ensure their support for the costly facilities. Trump said that to make them more popular, data center operators should pay the community, "and/or individuals within the community, a 'dividend.'" "I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck. MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!! GREAT FOR THE U.S.A.," the president said in a post on Truth Social. Data centers have become a hot-button issue ahead of the midterm elections in November. Public opposition to the buildout of the facilities and their environmental impact has been growing, with multiple states considering moratoriums. AI infrastructure company Nebius is "100% in principle" having discussions about investing in communities, the company's Chief Revenue Officer Marc Boroditsky told CNBC when asked about Trump's suggestion of a dividend. There could be "some sort of way where the rewards are actually funneled back to the community," Boroditsky told CNBC's Arjun Kharpal on the sidelines of Nvidia 's GTC Berlin conference. "We see it today in terms of the tax revenue that are arriving. I could see something like a benefit of some sort that's more direct economic opportunity for the community as well," he said. Boroditsky added: "A dividend is being paid in different forms — investing in education, job development, overall economic development. The concept that the president identified... it's not crazy to consider something like that." Data center stocks have also come under pressure this week amid growing concerns about the financial health of the sector. As the AI infrastructure buildout grows more costly, companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance deals. When it comes to investing in infrastructure underpinning the technology, HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery advised discernment over an all-in approach. "One has to be selective," Elhedery told CNBC's Dan Murphy on Tuesday. "You have to look at the quality of the tenancy agreements. You have to look at the pricing of these contracts. Not all of them are of that level of virtuosity that you can support strongly. Some of them may be more challenging." Much of the concern centers around water usage , power consumption , electricity prices, and the sheer amount of space that some centers require. Access to power is a major constraint on the sector, as power grids in the U.S. and Europe become overwhelmed with applications from large energy users like data centers. "Energy is always a bottleneck, and trying to find powered land and areas that we can build large-scale AI factories is a big focus for us," Chase Lochmiller, CEO of compute infrastructure firm Crusoe, told CNBC Wednesday in Berlin. "Increasingly there's a lot of policy permitting and just working through local communities to make sure that everything can come online effectively," he said. Trump, a long-time supporter of data centers, said Wednesday that he has been watching them "very closely" and has now come to a "very strong conclusion." "New and large, in some cases gigantic, Data enters are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid, and therefore there is electric price increase. In fact, there could be a substantial decrease," Trump said, in a post around 1.37 a.m. ET. In some cases, data centers can operate as flexible loads, adjusting their electricity use to help stabilize the grid. Hyperscalers have secured deals where they agree to help finance badly needed updates to local power grids. However, some experts have warned that the AI boom will ultimately result in higher electricity prices . events.title: Former chief executive banned after misconduct led to £4m losses in high-risk investments
events.summary: The FCA has banned Jeffrey Dawkins, the former chief executive of Vector Wealth Ltd, after he dishonestly acted as a front for a disqualified director using the company to sell high-risk bonds. Mr Dawkins has also been fined nearly £270,000.In 2019, Mr Dawkins sold Vector Wealth to a disqualified director who described himself as CEO and wanted to use Vector Wealth’s FCA-authorised status to sell mini-bonds.Mr Dawkins told the FCA he was still in charge, but the new “CEO” was really running the firm. This deception allowed the disqualified director to promote mini-bonds using the legitimacy of the firm to make them appear safer than they were.The disqualified director and Kadir Kanizi, a former senior manager at Vector Wealth, promoted the bonds but investors were not properly warned about the risks.Investors put in £105,000 on average, with one investing £1.1 million. Before seeing the marketing material, they had to confirm they were high net worth or sophisticated investors. Investors are expected to lose about £4 million.The FCA has banned Mr Kanizi from senior management roles. He was fined for failing to make sure consumers were properly warned about the risks.Therese Chambers, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said, 'Jeffrey Dawkins acted as a front man for a banned director, helping high-risk investments look safer than they were.'Mr Dawkins and Mr Kanizi allowed misleading promotions to draw in investors, many of whom now face significant losses. Mini-bonds and similar investments are very high risk, and people should be extremely cautious.'The FCA has warned about the risks of investing in mini-bonds and loan notes. A loan note or mini-bond usually involves lending money to a company for a set period in return for interest. If that company fails, consumers could lose every penny.Consumers need to be alert to the risk of harm and protect themselves using the tools available, like the FCA Firm Checker.Notes to editorsRead the final notices for Jeffrey Dawkins and Kadir Kanizi.There is statutory obligation to report the change in control of authorised firms.Vector Wealth Limited was formed as Fifth Quarter Asset Management (UK) Limited on 23 March 2012. Mr Dawkins held authorised positions at the firm from 5 March 2013. Vector Wealth’s authorisation ended on 28 January 2025.Mr Kanizi was appointed as a director on 22 September 2020 and was approved by the FCA on 6 September 2021.The disqualified director was banned from acting as a company director for 12 years in August 2014.The penalty in respect of Mr Dawkins includes a multiplier to reflect the seriousness of the conduct. It also includes an uplift for failing to cooperate with the FCA’s investigation. The full calculation is set out at section 6 of the Final Notice. Mr Dawkins has also been ordered to pay £57,298 plus interest (£68,257) of the proceeds he received from selling Vector Wealth and continuing to act as its director and approved person.The FCA has calculated that Kadir Kanizi should have been fined £80,096 but it reduced the penalty to £20,000 after he demonstrated that it would cause serious financial hardship. In the interest of maximising the funds available to be distributed to investors, the FCA agreed not to enforce the penalty if the same amount was made available by Mr Kanizi to Vector Wealth’s liquidators. He has also agreed to complete consumer duty training before taking up any future role in financial services.Investors who bought bonds through Vector Wealth should contact the firm’s liquidator and check the FCA website for updates.The FCA has investigated the matters that fall within its remit. The FCA may share relevant information with other law enforcement agencies where appropriate. Confirming or comment on individual referrals could risk affecting ongoing investigations.The FCA now actively removes the unutilised permissions of firms. Historically firms were expected to voluntarily request cancellation of unused permissions.The FCA permanently banned the marketing of speculative illiquid securities, including mini-bonds and loan notes, to retail investors from 1 January 2021.Anyone approached about loan notes, mini-bonds or similar high-risk investments should stop and check before investing, especially where adverts promise big, fixed returns or make the investment look simple and safe. Use the FCA’s Firm Checker and Warning List before handing over any money.

events.title: NVIDIA and Supply Chain Partners Expand Capacity to Accelerate AI Infrastructure Buildout
events.summary: News Summary: Substrate agreements with IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron Technology Corporation will, in aggregate, drive a 2.5x increase in capacity over the next three years. Amkor plans to increase its advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028. KYEC will build new facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. SPIL is targeting to increase its optical-engine capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced plans with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform. Working with Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and Unimicron Technology Corporation, NVIDIA is enabling new and existing suppliers to expand critical manufacturing capabilities across substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines, strengthening the resiliency and redundancy of NVIDIA’s global supply chain. “We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our supply chain partners are the world’s best manufacturers. I’m grateful they are expanding capacity around the globe to scale production and help us deliver the AI supercomputing systems powering this new industrial revolution.” Expanding Substrate Capacity to Support Volume Growth NVIDIA plans to increase substrate capacity for its products by 2.5x over the next three years. The agreements below will contribute to this capacity expansion, with more underway. Under an agreement signed and announced earlier this year by IBIDEN, NVIDIA is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance to support IBIDEN’s Ono Plant in Japan. The expansion targets capacity reaching 3x current levels at the plant, with additional capacity expected to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is joining NVIDIA’s substrate supply chain, bringing immediate capacity from its existing operations in South Korea. The collaboration also supports facility upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea. By 2028, production allocated to NVIDIA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ total annual package substrate production capacity. NVIDIA is supporting Unimicron’s KF substrate manufacturing expansion in Taiwan with a capacity reservation agreement. The expansion is expected to begin adding capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028. Scaling Advanced Packaging for Next-Generation Platforms NVIDIA and Amkor plan to expand advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, targeting a greater than 300% increase in interposer wafer capacity by the end of 2028. The planned capacity expansion, alongside Amkor’s development of new manufacturing facilities in South Korea, will support higher production volumes for NVIDIA’s current and next-generation platforms. Expanding Semiconductor Testing and Strengthening US Manufacturing NVIDIA expects its total semiconductor testing capacity to double from calendar 2026 to 2027, supported by buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan and Singapore. NVIDIA’s $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC will support new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027. In Singapore, expanded testing operations are expected to begin high-volume production in February 2027. Creating the Infrastructure for Co-Packaged Optics NVIDIA and SPIL plan to expand manufacturing capacity in Taiwan for optical engines used in co-packaged optics, supporting the growing connectivity requirements of large-scale computing infrastructure. The expansion targets an increase of 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. ]]>

events.title: Giant tunnel proposed to tackle Windermere sewage discharges
events.summary: United Utilities, Environment Agency and local campaigners say 12-mile tunnel could take sewage away from England’s largest lake Plans are under way for a new giant tunnel to transport sewage away from Windermere, England’s largest lake. Windermere, in the Lake District, has suffered from widespread raw sewage and bacterial pollution driven by discharges from United Utilities . Campaigners say this pollution has caused more frequent toxic blue-green algal blooms, with the public advised to avoid swimming in the lake. Modelling indicates the climate crisis will exacerbate these challenges, with the catchment expected to experience more intense rainfall over the coming years, placing further pressure on the wastewater infrastructure. A new project, backed by United Utilities, the Environment Agency and local campaigners, has set out a vision to end sewage discharges into the lake by building an 12-mile (19km) tunnel to transport sewage away from the lake. The water company said the use of tunnelling techniques would minimise the disruption to local communities. Windermere is at the heart of the Lake District Unesco world heritage site and has been the inspiration for poets, storytellers and lyricists for generations, with an estimated 17.7 million people visiting every year. The treated effluent would then be discharged into either the River Leven or the Irish Sea at Ulverston. It is estimated the project will cost £3.6bn, with United Utilities to seek permission from the government to raise customer bills to pay for it. It said the programme could add up to £3.17 a month to water bills in 2035. The project will now enter the detailed design phase during which specialised engineers will work out the technicalities of the build, which is expected to take two years. If granted permission to raise bills to pay for the project, United Utilities said the project could be complete within seven years and would provide a “one and done” solution with an immediate impact. The planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essential Matt Staniek, a campaigner at Save Windermere, which is a partner on the project, said creating the feasibility report had involved weekly meetings over 15 months. Staniek, who has been calling for the end of sewage discharges into the lake for more than five years, said he was concerned at first about partnering with the company causing the pollution, but said they were the only people who could actually fix it. “This has demonstrated that it is possible not to dump sewage in Lake Windermere,” he said. In planning for the project, the team considered the transformation of Lake Annecy in France, which is widely recognised as one of the cleanest lakes in Europe. In the 1950s, Annecy faced similar pollution problems, but the authorities invested in long-term infrastructural improvements to eliminate the sewage discharges. “This is up to the government now. The plan is there, it’s in place, we’re not going to stop until Andy Burnham is on the shores of Lake Windermere with a spade announcing that the construction has begun on this project,” Staniek said.

events.title: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents
events.summary: Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget. Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets. Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Crusoe Cloud serves leading model and application builders across EMEA, including Base44, Gradium, LTX and Wonderful. Aleria, Cassava Technologies , Firebird , G42 , Radiant, SWI Compute and Vultr are also developing and expanding NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure across Europe, the Nordics, Africa and Central Asia. Regional capacity from AI clouds combines the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform , including NVIDIA Vera Rubin, NVIDIA BlueField and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, giving customers greater choice and control over where workloads and data reside while advancing sovereign computing services and economic growth. Open: Models and Libraries, From Training to Inference Across the ecosystem, AI clouds are expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure and services for developers to build applications with open models and libraries. This new capacity supports model training, fine-tuning for specialized tasks and inference at scale, including applications deployed at the edge. For production inference, Nebius has adopted NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, using Spectrum-X Ethernet networking to integrate it with Vera Rubin NVL72 on Nebius Token Factory. The combination will bring faster token generation to latency-sensitive applications and agentic systems through the platform’s managed serverless and dedicated endpoints and familiar application programming interfaces. For robotics and physical AI, Nebius offers a purpose-built AI cloud solution that includes its full-stack Physical AI Workbench. Robotics companies including Rhoda AI , RoboForce and Sereact are building on the platform. The company also launched three NVIDIA retail agent blueprints — covering inventory, store operations, and fine-tuning —- into early access on Nebius infrastructure. Nebius is expanding its cloud services widely across the continent with its Physical AI Living Lab, and in Germany as a computer supplier for the Next Frontier Challenge of SPRIND, the Federal Agency for Breakthrough Innovation. Baseten has developed a specialized model for code-review routing with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning used by CodeRabbit. Through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, CodeRabbit improved routing agreement from 75.8% to 80.7% while reducing estimated inference costs by 50% for the evaluated workload. The results demonstrate how AI developers can customize NVIDIA open models for specialized tasks while improving accuracy and inference efficiency. Fireworks and Era4 are partnering to bring open models to enterprises across the U.K. and Europe. The collaboration combines Fireworks ’ model training and inference platform with direct liquid-cooled capacity powered by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs at Era4’s Chesterfield facility, supporting plans for enterprise AI solutions in financial services, insurance and life sciences. Mistral is expanding its NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure to support model training, customization and inference. The expansion includes NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure planned for delivery in 2027. Trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral -operated European data centers, Mistral Large 4 is the company’s latest frontier multimodal model, advancing capabilities across coding, agentic workflows and multimodal understanding. Verda plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin, continuing to promote open weight models with NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos already in production, and using the NVIDIA Dynamo open source framework for inference optimization. Safe: Secure Boundaries for AI Agents, From Silicon to Software As developers connect models to tools and business systems, they also need controls over what agents can access and do. Announced at GTC Berlin, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture with support from AI cloud ecosystem partners. Built on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime software, the architecture is designed to give organizations full-stack control to deploy AI agents with clear boundaries around what agents can access and do. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 for model inference, NVIDIA Vera CPUs with OpenShell for agent harnesses and tool use, and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. Each play a distinct role in delivering that control, working together so agents can achieve what they’re meant to do without moving beyond the boundaries people set for them. Partners including Aleria , Baseten , Cassava , CoreWeave , Crusoe , DigitalOcean , Firebird , Fireworks, Firmus , G42 , GMI Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Lightning AI, Nebius , Nscale , Radiant Verda and Vultr are supporting the OpenShell Reference Architecture to enable secure agentic deployments for their customers. Together, European AI clouds are connecting regional infrastructure investment with the work of building and deploying AI. Expanded capacity gives builders more places to run workloads.

events.title: Europe’s Industrial Leaders Reinvent Engineering and Manufacturing With NVIDIA
events.summary: To increase productivity, accelerate innovation and create new opportunities for economic growth, Europe’s industrial leaders are tapping NVIDIA CUDA-X and Omniverse libraries , as well as NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron open models, across the engineering and manufacturing lifecycle. Bringing those capabilities together on the factory floor, the NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX) is now available in early access on GitHub , providing a path for developers to build and deploy always-on factory manager agents that coordinate work across machines, and specialist agents focused on use cases such as visual inspection, root cause analysis, report generation and fleet management. These agents can connect to frontier models, including NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron, and foundational knowledge including computer-aided design, product lifecycle management, simulation software, and IT and operational technology systems. Building on the FOX blueprint enables the ecosystem to build industrial agents that monitor factory operations in real time, correlate visual findings and machine logs to investigate problems, and coordinate responses. With Cosmos in-context learning, these agents can adapt using examples and documentation, without fine-tuning. Siemens is integrating agents built using FOX into Intelligence Center X, its agentic enterprise system, to help identify root causes and coordinate factory operations, for estimated cost savings of 20%. Siemens’ Process Preparation X agents use NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory tools and skills to generate defect images for circuit-board inspection. At its Erlangen electronics factory, Siemens used this approach to reduce calibration time of inspection processes by 40%. Accelerating Engineering From the First Design NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries accelerate simulation, giving engineers faster feedback to explore design alternatives before committing to physical prototypes. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is releasing cuDSS for general availability , accelerating the demanding calculations behind the complex simulations of structural stress, fluid flow, electromagnetic fields and semiconductor device behavior. Mercedes-Benz uses Siemens’ Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on NVIDIA GPUs to compare vehicle designs through faster aerodynamic simulations. In factories, the company applies NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and the Metropolis VSS blueprint to build agents for vehicle inspection and windshield assembly verification, detecting deviations and ensuring consistently high quality. Cadence is benchmarking automotive fluid-dynamics workloads on NVIDIA GPUs to assess opportunities for faster design iteration, while Autodesk brings the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo and Warp frameworks into NavPack, integrated with Autodesk Alias, to help designers like those at Bentley’s predict vehicle performance and iterate faster using simulation-trained AI. imec and Infineon are accelerating semiconductor simulation with Synopsys software and NVIDIA accelerated computing. Benchmarks of S-Litho on imec’s model show up to 40x speedup, while Infineon uses Sentaurus Device with NVIDIA CUDA libraries to achieve a 12x speedup in 3D breakdown simulation for next-generation power devices. Leonardo is working with Neural Concept on AI-driven aircraft design, tapping NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bring aircraft geometry and aerodynamic simulation results together. Car manufacturers use Dassault Systèmes ’ LEO & AURA Virtual Companions, powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, and orchestrating CATIA AI Agents & SIMULIA AI Agents with SIMULIA solvers, accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, to rapidly design and virtually test vehicle doors before building physical prototypes. UniversalAGI is working with Saab to protect sailors from life-threatending wave impacts at sea, using UniversalAGI’s Latent Interaction Field Transformer physics AI foundation models with accelerated processing by NVIDIA Warp to evaluate thousands of wave conditions and headings in real time instead of days. These capabilities enable vessels to anticipate dangerous motion and autonomously select safer routes to avoid putting sailors at risk, while NVIDIA Omniverse libraries help visualize vessel behavior at sea. PhysicsX is working with GB1, Britain’s America’s Cup team , on AI-powered yacht design, using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to visualize hull geometry and pressure fields, while Fermioniq ’s Sofia agent helps Deltares and Dutch ministries model river flow by translating natural-language requests into simulation solvers built on NVIDIA Warp. Mistral plans to use CUDA-X, Warp and Omniverse libraries to accelerate physics simulation and generate training data for engineering AI models. Testing Factories and Robots Virtually NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac libraries enable digital twins and robotics simulation , helping manufacturers evaluate production systems and robot behavior before making changes on the factory floor. Audi uses a battery-production digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to test production concepts before physical equipment is available. The company is also working with Dassault Systèmes and Agile Robots to simulate and validate mobile humanoid robots and logistics processes in DELMIA virtual twins built with Omniverse libraries. Schaeffler is integrating digital twins of its humanoid actuators — components that move robot joints — with NVIDIA Isaac simulation frameworks, helping its robotics partners evaluate component behavior in simulation and reduce physical testing. Wandelbots uses NOVA with Isaac Sim , built on Omniverse and OpenUSD, to validate assembly workflows digitally and prepare applications for physical robots. Falkor , a KONGSBERG company, is integrating agents and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries into its platform. With Microsoft Azure NCv6 virtual machines powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, agents with spatial intelligence combine engineering data, operating information and 3D equipment geometry to see, simulate and reason over industrial facilities, supporting inspection and maintenance use cases across the process and energy industries. The same simulation approach extends to AI infrastructure. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA , is developing an AI factory digital twin built for Nscale with Omniverse libraries to help engineers compare power, cooling and equipment configurations before making physical changes. events.title: NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations
events.summary: NVIDIA cuDSS, launched today in general availability, is an NVIDIA CUDA-X library that shifts a critical part of engineering and scientific simulations onto GPUs. Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test. NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost. Industry leaders are already integrating NVIDIA cuDSS into their tools to transform workflows for their end customers: Applied Materials: With cuDSS, Applied Materials accelerated sparse solves in Ginestra, its physics-based, defect-centric simulation platform, by up to 10x versus CPU-only approaches, speeding exploration of semiconductor materials and device reliability. COMSOL: Using COMSOL Multiphysics with NVIDIA cuDSS on NVIDIA accelerated computing, ZEISS SMT achieved a measured 4x speedup in an EUV lithography plasma simulation benchmark, completing the full simulation in six days and 14 hours. Cadence : Uses cuDSS in its Celsius software to accelerate simulations of heat, structural stress and warpage in advanced chips and 3D chip designs, helping customers including Nokia analyze complex designs faster. Dassault Systèmes : Dassault Systèmes reports an 8-10x speedup using cuDSS within its Abaqus structural and computer simulation technology electromagnetic solvers for performance-critical simulations across industries. Siemens : Siemens uses cuDSS in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to accelerate simulations of structures in fluid-structure interaction workflows. Synopsys : Synopsys uses cuDSS in its Sentaurus Device simulator tool to accelerate simulations of advanced logic, memory and power chips, helping Infineon model increasingly complex devices faster. As simulation workloads grow in size and complexity, cuDSS can scale out of the box from individual workstations to large computing clusters. Developers can integrate cuDSS into existing engineering, scientific and optimization software offerings, bringing GPU acceleration to tools already used by engineers and researchers. They can use cuDSS through C, C++, Python and Fortran interfaces. Learn more about cuDSS by visiting the NVIDIA demo booth and Dassault Systèmes booth at GTC Berlin. events.title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure
events.summary: NVIDIA builds tools to enable safe agents across the stack . The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, announced today , is part of NVIDIA’s growing portfolio of technologies that enables organizations to safely deploy agents at scale. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is the infrastructure layer that protects the models and data those agents depend on while running. Today, NVIDIA is expanding that layer with Confidential Bare Metal, a new deployment option with NVIDIA Confidential Computing that enables frontier model builders to run sensitive workloads on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data. NVIDIA is introducing new platform security controls that protect data in transit, measure platform integrity and enforce hardware-level access restrictions. These new controls let frontier model builders use bare-metal instances to own and operate their bespoke software stack, including host and platform infrastructure software, when operating on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure across third-party cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure. NVIDIA Confidential Computing now offers a converged security architecture with three deployment options: Confidential Bare Metal for bare-metal infrastructure Confidential Containers for Kubernetes environments Confidential Virtual Machines for virtualized environments Organizations can match the right model to their trust boundaries and operating requirements. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is also expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems and will integrate with NVIDIA DSX OS as a reference architecture for cloud providers building AI factories. Confidential Bare Metal gives supported providers a path to serve high-value workloads that require strong model and data privacy protections. For model builders, the expanding ecosystem offers more geographic, sovereign and operational options for scaling training and inference worldwide. Cohere plans to integrate Confidential Bare Metal into Cohere Model Vault, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing trusted execution environments to extend hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU — protecting models and data in memory and across interconnects during execution. “Enterprises trust Cohere to provide a secure and confidential platform for inference,” said Phil Blunsom, chief technology officer at Cohere. “With NVIDIA Confidential Computing in Cohere Model Vault, we’re extending hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU, protecting customer data in memory and across interconnects during execution.” Google Cloud is extending support for Confidential Bare Metal to A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. These will combine non-virtualized NVIDIA accelerated computing with cryptographic protection for training data and model intellectual property. “Google Cloud introduces Confidential Bare Metal to provide AI labs with hardware-isolated, non-virtualized compute environments and end-to-end cryptographic protection. Our A4X instances, built using NVIDIA Confidential Computing, preserve the privacy of user data, protect model IP, provide top-line serving performance,” said Andrés Lagar-Cavilla, distinguished engineer and AI infrastructure security lead at Google Cloud. Confidential Computing Expands Across the NVIDIA Platform NVIDIA Confidential Computing uses hardware-rooted isolation and cryptographic attestation to help protect models and data during execution. Support now extends to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL72 — bringing Confidential Computing to NVL72 rack-scale systems — as well as x86-based NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems. CoreWeave , Firmus , GMI Cloud , Google Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Microsoft Azure Infrastructure, Nebius , Nscale and Vultr support NVIDIA Confidential Computing deployments. Global systems partners including Cisco , Dell Technologies , HPE , Lenovo, Supermicro and Bull will support these capabilities with NVIDIA-Certified Systems . NVIDIA DSX OS will support all NVIDIA Confidential Computing modes, giving cloud providers a software foundation for building and operating AI factories that support confidential workloads. events.title: A CMO was horrified by how ChatGPT described her company. Here’s how she’s fixing it.
events.summary: Ameresco CMO Leila Dillon has been shaking up the energy solutions provider's AI visibility strategy. Ameresco A version of this post appears in CMO Insider. Sign up for Business Insider's marketing newsletter . When Ameresco CMO Leila Dillon asked ChatGPT and other AI answer engines to describe what her company did, she was shocked by the results. The publicly traded company is an energy infrastructure provider, helping power the rapidly growing AI buildout, as well as military bases and municipal facilities. But the AI chatbots were outdated in their responses, frequently referring to it simply as a cleantech or renewable energy business — areas it still operates in, but are less of a focus — or citing smaller projects it worked on years ago. "It was quite horrifying," Dillon told CMO Insider. "We were like, 'That's not at all who we are.'" Dillon set about overhauling the company's messaging and how it structured its marketing content to better reflect its business. The work has begun to take effect. Ameresco tracked how often AI chatbots mentioned the company in response to 50 questions that potential customers and investors might ask. It appeared in 61% of those answers in 2026, up from 43% in 2025, according to the company. As more consumers turn to platforms like ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, Anthropic's Claude , and Microsoft's Copilot to research companies and products, marketers are racing to hone their generative engine optimization (GEO) strategies to ensure their brands appear prominently and accurately in AI-generated answers. "I used to Google everything that I wanted to know about," Dillon said. "I barely use Google anymore. I use Copilot, and I get better results." In a January survey from the Interactive Advertising Bureau, 73% of US brand and agency buyers said they planned to devote more time or resources to optimizing content for AI-generated answers in 2026, compared with last year. In a separate survey of US marketing professionals conducted by Semrush, an AI and search visibility platform, in April, 30% of marketers said AI search tools had described their brands inaccurately. The rush by marketers to get up to speed with GEO has spawned a cottage industry of AI search experts and tools promising quick fixes. But with AI companies constantly updating their models, marketers are in a phase of constant experimentation as they scramble to figure out what actually influences the chatbots. "There's no one shot that fits all to solve that for you," Dillon said. An AI audit identified 47 areas for improvement In January 2025, Dillon's team and its PR agency, Greenough, began auditing how often Ameresco appeared in AI-generated answers to 50 prompts — such as, "What are the top energy infrastructure providers in the US?" — on platforms including ChatGPT and Claude. The prompts reflected questions that investors and prospective customers, including people from universities and utilities, might ask AI chatbots. The audit identified 47 areas for improvement, including how Ameresco described its business across its website, social media, press releases, and executive communications. "You name it, we were doing it wrong," Dillon said. Ameresco began rolling out a new corporate brand identity in July this year, reflecting its broader reorganization around two business pillars: power infrastructure and buildings and public infrastructure. It had laid the groundwork for the new corporate brand reveal by making several changes to its content strategy. Those included: Updating its corporate boilerplate from "a leading cleantech integrator specializing in energy efficiency and renewable energy" to "a leading energy infrastructure company," reflecting the new positioning across its marketing and communications. Refreshing its awards submission strategy to lead with its power infrastructure projects, and announcing each win with a press release that appears on wire services and industry trade publications. Introducing Q&A-style content formats, designed to make the information easier for AI chatbots to interpret. Creating more content designed for different customer groups, such as data center operators or school facilities managers, rather than relying on generic marketing materials. Launching a video content series called "Energy Benefits Unlocked," highlighting the tangible results Ameresco's projects accomplished for its customers. Introducing quarterly AI visibility tracking audits across the 50 different prompts, reflecting its different audiences, and adding competitor comparisons. A constantly moving target The strategy appears to be paying off in some ways. Ameresco said organic traffic to its website rose 50% in the 12 months to June 2026. Dillon said it's still too early to assess precisely how those gains translate into business results, though she believes the GEO work is helping the marketing team hit its targets more quickly. The company is scheduled to report its third-quarter earnings on November 9. Dillon said the rapid changes in AI mean the work is never really finished. Ameresco regularly revisits its AI visibility scores and has invested in training the marketing team, which shares tips, tricks, and their "epic AI fails" in its weekly meetings. "One of the main themes is that what happened last week is not what you're going to get this week; it's changing that quickly," Dillon said. "You don't just update your website and say: Done, woo, all set," she added. Read the original article on Business Insider

events.title: UK approves development of Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea
events.summary: The decision has drawn sharp criticism from left-wing politicians and environmentalists. The United Kingdom’s government has approved a natural gas project off the coast of Scotland, as the Labour government seeks to balance its climate goals with energy security concerns. Energy Minister Miatta Fahnbulleh said on Wednesday that the Jackdaw gasfield would begin supplying energy to UK homes by the end of the month and would help to boost the country’s energy security. list 1 of 3 ‘Totally reliant on Mother Nature’: UK drought raises water security fears list 2 of 3 ‘Nature can recover’: Inside the race to rescue world’s crisis-hit wildlife list 3 of 3 Why a North Sea oilfield is emerging as British PM Burnham’s big test The government said the North Sea project would increase UK gas production by about 6 percent at its peak. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the decision will “protect hundreds of jobs and help keep millions of homes warm”, but stressed it would not hinder the government’s targets on renewable energy. The government also announced a New Energy Wealth Fund, which will invest in renewable and low-carbon energy projects as part of the green transition. The fund has been established with an initial 2 billion pounds ($2.7bn), with plans to raise additional funds through tax revenues from North Sea oil and gas. Higher energy prices amid the Russia-Ukraine war and the United States-Israel war on Iran have weighed on households and businesses, dragging on Britain’s economy. Fahnbulleh told UK radio station LBC that the development of Jackdaw would not bring down household energy bills. “I think it’s really important that we’re honest about this,” Fahnbulleh said. “That was not a consideration in the decision because it won’t mean cheaper bills. This was about energy security.” The announcement has drawn criticism from left-wing politicians and environmental groups. Zack Polanski, the leader of the opposition Green Party, described the decision as “climate vandalism”. “Surreal to hear [the] energy secretary try and say this is a ‘pragmatic decision’,” Polanski wrote in a post on X. “It will do nothing to lower bills. It will do lots for the profits of the oil and gas companies. And will continue us further down the path of floods and wildfires.” Environmental group Greenpeace said the decision showed “the toxic grip fossil fuel lobbyists still hold over our energy policy”. “True pragmatism means severing our reliance on expensive oil and gas that leaves British households broke, supercharges extreme weather, and leaves our energy security at the mercy of petrostates,” said Ami McCarthy, head of politics at Greenpeace UK.

events.title: WW1 to Houthis: British jets for Saudi Arabia build on long military bond
events.summary: The UK’s deployment of jets to defend Saudi Arabia is the latest chapter in a military relationship older than the kingdom itself. The United Kingdom has announced it will deploy Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets to help defend Saudi Arabia from missile and drone attacks by Yemen’s Houthis, the armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God). The jets will play a “defensive role”, the British Ministry of Defence (MoD) said in a statement on Tuesday, adding that they will not carry out attacks against the Iranian-backed armed group. list 1 of 4 Iran sees ‘false flag’ operations after UK blames IRGC for airbase incident list 2 of 4 UK spy chief says Iran is stepping up targeting of military bases list 3 of 4 UK to deploy Typhoon jets to help defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks list 4 of 4 UK police rearrest two men on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence The move comes amid heavy fighting between the Houthis and Yemen’s internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia. In recent weeks, the Houthis have carried out missile and drone attacks against the kingdom, including oil facilities and Riyadh’s main airport , while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the Yemeni government has launched air attacks on Houthi positions. The UK’s decision to send jets to assist Saudi Arabia marks just the latest chapter in a partnership that stretches back more than a century, to a treaty signed during the First World War, years before the Saudi kingdom was founded. So what is the UK sending, and how did the two countries become so closely bound? Fighter jets, an A400M transport aircraft and advisers. The ministry said it was also extending air-to-air refuelling , which it previously agreed to provide for Saudi air operations, including those to degrade Houthi military targets in Yemen. How far back does the UK-Saudi relationship go? In December 1915, Sir Percy Cox, a senior British official in the Gulf, concluded the Treaty of Darin with King Abdulaziz Ibn Saud, then ruler of Nejd in central Arabia, according to India Office records held by the UK’s National Archives. In return, he allied with Britain against the Ottoman Empire, and Britain backed him with cash and weapons. In May 1927, Britain signed a new treaty with him at Jeddah, according to an India Office memorandum. King Abdulaziz founded the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in 1932. When did UK-Saudi arms deals begin? In May 1966, Saudi Arabia signed contracts to buy 40 Lightning fighter jets and 25 jet trainers from the British Aircraft Corporation, along with a radar system, according to a US Department of State memo from the time. Even then, Yemen was part of the picture. In 1962, the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen was overthrown in a military coup and the Yemen Arab Republic was established. Egypt sent troops to back the republican government, while Saudi Arabia and Jordan armed and funded royalist forces trying to restore the Imam. By 1966, the civil war had reached a stalemate. Meanwhile, Britain was facing rebellion from Soviet- and Egypt-backed nationalist groups over its control of Aden and southern Yemen. Britain ultimately withdrew in 1967. In 1966, Saudi Arabia’s defence minister, Prince Sultan, asked the UK to supply an RAF fighter squadron to fly under Saudi colours if fighting resumed in Yemen, according to declassified US State Department records. Britain instead offered fighter jets flown by British pilots, and said it was ready to send an RAF squadron of Lightning interceptors for a short period if required. In the end, Saudi Arabia accepted the jets and civilian pilots, and the RAF squadron was not needed, the records show. BAE Systems, then the British Aircraft Corporation, says its ties with Saudi Arabia date back to 1966, and in 1973, the two governments signed a memorandum of understanding naming the company as prime contractor. In 1985, the two governments signed an oil-for-arms agreement, known as Al-Yamamah, for Tornado and Hawk jets. The Reuters news agency has described the Al-Yamamah deals as the largest export contracts in British history. Saudi Arabia set aside up to 600,000 barrels of oil a day to pay for Tornado jets and other equipment. The UK’s Serious Fraud Office investigated corruption allegations linked to the deal from 2004, but dropped the inquiry in December 2006, according to a House of Lords judgement. The attorney general, Lord Goldsmith, cited the need to safeguard national security. Has Britain fought from Saudi soil before? When Iraq invaded Kuwait in August 1990, King Fahd of Saudi Arabia asked friendly governments for help. On August 11, 12 RAF Tornado fighters flew from Akrotiri in Cyprus to Dhahran in Saudi Arabia, according to the RAF Museum. Further RAF Tornado detachments were set up at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia in October 1990, and at Dhahran in January 1991, the museum’s records show.
